decisions.quote:
In the present article we report a direct replication of Cialdini et al.’s (1975) DITF

technique. Overall, the data were consistent with the findings obtained by Cialdini et al.

(1975). In fact, the agreement rates were similarly high as those in the original study even

though we ran the study almost half a century later in another country on another continent.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding agree on 'successful'. The authors state an explicit overall verdict that their replication data were consistent with and yielded similarly high compliance rates as Cialdini et al. (1975), with all preregistered tests matching the original direction and predictions; a difference between the two control conditions emerged only in a non-preregistered exploratory analysis altering exclusion rules and does not override the overall replication verdict under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1.

decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding classify the study as a replication. The authors collected new experimental data from a fresh sample of 410 participants (final N = 391) in Germany to directly re-test Study 3 of Cialdini et al. (1975).
